title: Chase App Won't Open on Android? Why 'Developer Options' Blocks It & How to Fix [2026]
content:
You tap the Chase icon on your Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel, or Android smartphone, and instead of the familiar blue login dashboard, the app instantly crashes to your home screen or presents a blunt security warning: **"Device does not meet security requirements"** or **"App cannot run in this environment."**

Many users assume their phone has malware or that the latest Chase update is broken. In reality, modern financial banking apps incorporate strict **tamper-detection anti-hooking libraries** (like Promon SHIELD or DexGuard). 

If your phone has **Developer Options**, **USB Debugging**, or **Wireless ADB** enabled, Chase systematically shuts down to prevent memory inspection attacks.

Here is how to disable the offending developer toggles and restore your Chase banking app in 60 seconds.

## Why Does Developer Mode Block the Chase Mobile App?

**Chase blocks execution when Developer Options are enabled because Android's debugging bridge (ADB) allows external computers to inspect memory buffers, capture encrypted screen contents, and inject modified bytecode.** To comply with banking security standards, Chase mandates a production-only operating environment.

| Security Trigger | Technical Risk Evaluated by Chase |
| :--- | :--- |
| **USB Debugging** | Memory inspection and automated screen taps |
| **Wireless Debugging** | Local Wi-Fi network packet sniffing |
| **Mock Locations** | GPS spoofing for geographical risk evaluations |
| **Fix Time** | 1 Minute |

> 💡 **The Reality:** Even if you only enabled Developer Options once months ago to speed up window animation scales or test Bluetooth audio codecs, the active developer flag remains visible to Chase's security scanner until toggled off.

## How to Disable Developer Options on Android (Samsung & Google Pixel)

### For Samsung Galaxy Devices (One UI):
1. Open your phone's **Settings**.
2. Scroll to the very bottom of the menu.
3. Locate **Developer options** (positioned directly below *About phone*).
4. Tap **Developer options**.
5. At the very top of the screen, toggle the master switch from **On** to **Off**.
6. Force close the Chase app from your Recent Apps menu and relaunch it.

### For Google Pixel, Motorola, and Stock Android:
1. Open phone **Settings**.
2. Tap **System** > **Developer options**.
3. Toggle the top switch to **Off**.
4. Restart your phone to flush Android's system runtime state.

## What to Do If the Chase App Still Crashes After Disabling Developer Mode

If you disabled Developer Options but Chase continues to shut down immediately on launch, one of these three secondary flags is lingering:

### 1. Clear Chase App Storage (Flush Cached Security State)
The Chase app may have cached the "untrusted device" flag in its local app data:
1. Go to **Settings** > **Apps** > **Chase**.
2. Tap **Storage & cache**.
3. Tap **Clear Cache**, then tap **Clear Storage** (Clear Data).
4. Open Chase. The app will initiate a fresh hardware integrity scan.

### 2. Check for "Accessibility Services" Monopolization
Malicious banking trojans frequently exploit Android Accessibility Services to read login credentials. Chase flags certain non-standard accessibility overlays:
1. Open **Settings** > **Accessibility**.
2. Review **Downloaded apps / Installed services**.
3. Temporarily turn off third-party macro apps (e.g., auto-clickers, third-party gesture navigators, third-party password managers).

### 3. Verify Play Protect Certification
If your Android phone was purchased refurbished, bootloader unlocked, or imported from overseas:
1. Open the **Google Play Store**.
2. Tap your **Profile Icon** > **Settings** > **About**.
3. Look at the bottom under **Play Protect certification**.
4. If it states *"Device is not certified"* or your bootloader is unlocked (Root / Magisk), Chase’s SafetyNet / Play Integrity API will permanently block the app.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Can I keep Developer Options on and still use Chase?**
**No.** Chase’s security architecture strictly enforces an all-or-nothing policy on Android. To use the official native Chase Mobile app, Developer Options must be toggled off during banking sessions.

**Can I access Chase through my phone's Chrome browser with Developer Options enabled?**
**Yes!** If you require Developer Options active for your work or hobbies, open [Google Chrome](/guides/chase-online-banking-not-working-on-chrome) or Firefox on your phone, navigate to `chase.com`, and sign in. The web portal does not inspect Android developer flags.

**Does disabling Developer Options reset my phone or delete photos?**
**No.** Disabling Developer Options simply hides advanced developer debugging tools. It has zero impact on your personal data, photos, text messages, or installed apps.
